title: Retire Chat V1 HTTP Endpoints and Sunset Associated Legacy Models - Migration Spec
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Product requirements document for planned retirement of the legacy /v1/chat endpoints and sunsetting the associated legacy model variants (chat-v1-small, chat-v1-medium). Provides migration guidance, timelines, acceptance criteria, and operational runbook for the change.
background: We maintain two generations of chat endpoints. The v1 endpoints are backed by older runtime paths and model variants that are more expensive to serve and lack structured output guarantees introduced in v2. Usage on v1 has been declining but a non-trivial set of customers and internal integrations still rely on it. Aligning customers to the v2 API and newer model variants will reduce maintenance burden, improve latency/cost, and unlock unified tooling. This PRD specifies how we retire v1 endpoints and related models with minimal customer disruption.
goals: 1) Decommission /v1/chat endpoints and retire chat-v1-* models with no critical incidents. 2) Provide clear, actionable migration paths and tooling for customers to move to /v2/chat and recommended model families. 3) Ensure monitoring, fallback policies, and rollback mechanisms during the rollout. 4) Reduce runtime complexity and maintenance surface by removing legacy kernel paths after deprecation window.
scope_included:
- Public API: /v1/chat endpoints and dependent model variants chat-v1-small and chat-v1-medium.
- SDK wrappers that call /v1/chat in official SDKs (Node, Python) — provide patched versions.
- Developer docs, changelog, and migration examples.
- Console routing rules and metrics that reference v1 routes.
scope_excluded:
- Private on-prem / VPC deployments where customers explicitly opt into extended support (handled via separate contract).
- Non-chat endpoints (embeddings, rerank) unless they reference v1 models directly; those will be handled by separate tickets.
- Internal experimental branches that are not productionized.
constraints:
- Must maintain SLA for existing customers during migration window.
- Cannot remove v1 from hosted control plane until SDK patches and major customers have migrated or opted into extended support.
- Public announcement at least 60 days before mandatory cutoff and individual outreach for high-usage customers.
- All acceptance tests and synthetic traffic must pass on v2-equivalent flows before removal.
stakeholders: PM: Aisha Patel; Eng (API/SDK): Liam O'Connor, Mei Chen; Runtime: Daniel Ruiz; Docs: Priya Singh; Customer Success: Mateo Alvarez; Legal: Claire Thompson; Sales: Irene Gomez
timeline:
- 2026-03-15: Public notice and deprecation blog post published.
- 2026-03-22 to 2026-04-12: SDK patch releases (Node/Python) with automatic redirection helpers and migration examples.
- 2026-04-01 to 2026-04-30: Customer outreach and assisted migrations for top 25 customers.
- 2026-05-01: Grace period ends for standard customers; v1 marked read-only for new keys.
- 2026-06-01: v1 endpoints disabled for hosted API; private deployments subject to contract-based support.
- 2026-07-01: Remove legacy runtime kernel paths after post-mortem window.
migration_steps: Publish detailed migration guide with examples: mapping v1 request fields to v2, typical prompt adjustments, and model recommendations.
Release SDKs that detect v1 usage and log guidance; provide a single-line command to convert calls to v2 when safe.
Add server-side compatibility layer: during window, allow v1 requests to auto-forward to v2 models with telemetry flagging and rate-limited warnings.
Provide a CLI audit tool for customers to scan codebases for hardcoded /v1/chat usage and highlight breakage risks.
Coordinate with Runtime to ensure chat-v2 recommended models (chat-moderate, chat-highperf) meet parity for key behaviors used by customers.
Execute a staged rollout: feature-flagged forwarding -> warning-only -> read-only -> disabled.
Offer migration assistance for top customers and a purchasable extended-support plan for private deployments.
Update Console UI, dashboards, and cost reports to reflect v2 as default and mark v1 as deprecated in the route selector.
communication_plan: Deprecation blog post and docs page published on 2026-03-15 with timeline and FAQs.
Email campaign segmented by usage: high-impact customers contacted individually by CSM and Solutions Engineering; medium/low usage receive automated migration steps.
In-product banners for accounts making /v1 calls, linking to migration guide and SDK patch notes.
Changelog entries for SDK releases and a single migration checklist repo in GitHub with sample PR diffs.
Support playbook for CS and Support engineers with common troubleshooting steps and escalation contacts.
acceptance_criteria: All public SDKs (Node, Python) have shipped patches that either transparently map safe v1 calls to v2 or clearly surface migration warnings.
Automated compatibility test suite demonstrates parity for top 50 sample prompts between v1 and recommended v2 models with <5% degradations in quality metrics where unavoidable.
No unresolved P0 incidents during the staged rollout. Any P1 regressions must have mitigation in place within SLA window.
Customer-facing docs and migration guide published and linked from Console and API docs.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Announcement (2026-03-15): Publish docs and start outreach.
Phase 1 - SDK and tooling (2026-03-22 to 2026-04-12): Release SDKs and scanning tools; enable silent forwarding behind flag for internal testing.
Phase 2 - Warning mode (2026-04-13 to 2026-04-30): For accounts still calling v1, inject telemetry and warnings in responses and Console banners.
Phase 3 - Read-only (2026-05-01 to 2026-05-31): Reject write-style operations (if applicable) and continue providing read-only fallback where safe. New keys cannot create v1 routes.
Phase 4 - Disable (2026-06-01): Turn off /v1/chat endpoints on hosted API and archive metrics. Follow separate contract for private deployments.
monitoring_and_rollback:
Pre-rollout: Create dashboards for v1 and v2 traffic, error rates, latency and cost per token.
During rollout: Monitor customer error spikes, SDK telemetry, and support tickets; maintain hotline to engineering on-call.
Rollback options: Re-enable forwarding flag if significant regressions appear; reinstate v1 routing for specific account IDs as temporary mitigation.
Post-disable: Keep archived logs for 90 days and a read-only compatibility snapshot for debugging; any permanent rollback requires cross-org signoff.
followups: Post-mortem within 2 weeks of disable date documenting migration success metrics and lessons learned.
Ticket to decommission legacy kernel and runtime code paths (ENG-xxxx).
Update internal KB and onboarding docs to remove references to v1.
